title: Telemetry-driven experimental lane controller with staged silent-fallback
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Enable low-risk experimentation lanes that can be silently backed out without user-visible failovers and with minimal manual intervention. This change introduces an 'experimental lane controller' that drives short-lived A/B/experimental cohorts using telemetry signal windows and an automatic 'silent-fallback' path that drains traffic to a stable variant when metric regressions are detected.

Design summary: The controller evaluates multiple signal classes (latency p50/p95, error-rate, token-quality proxy) in sliding windows and maintains a low-cost shadow bucket for replay-driven comparison. Instead of immediate public failovers, the silent-fallback routes experimental traffic into a quarantined warm lane (no public promotion) while keeping a replay log for post-mortem and auto-bisect. The controller exposes a policy DSL for thresholds and decay rates. Key features: 1) cohort-aware decision state with session affinity preservation; 2) telemetry-weighted gating that tolerates intermittent noise; 3) grace window backoff and exponential holdpoints to avoid oscillation; 4) a graceful drain sequence that preserves in-flight KV caches and avoids double-execution; 5) automatic creation of a diagnostic shadow snapshot when a fallback triggers.

Why this is different: Unlike previous staged-rollout controllers, this focuses on non-disruptive silent fallback (traffic remains served from stable variant) while capturing deterministic replay artifacts for developers. The goal is faster experimentation with low blast radius and reproducible rollbacks.

Implementation notes: Controller implemented as a new package pkg/controller/exp_lane with two major components: policy evaluator and traffic orchestrator. Policy evaluator runs in the control-plane loop and receives pre-aggregated metrics from the telemetry ingestion API. Traffic orchestrator issues route changes via the existing servegraph API, but with new 'quarantine' route semantics. Added lightweight local replay writer that stores deterministic request fingerprints to the replay store (S3-backed). All new config is guarded behind the feature flag runtime.experimental_lanes (default: off).

Testing and validation: Unit tests for policy edge cases and hysteresis behavior included. Integration harness exercises session-affinity preservation and drain sequence with synthetic traces. Load tests run in benchmark-lab (bench/exp-lane-load) to measure overhead; CPU overhead under 1% at 10k rps. Perf regressions are instrumented and compared against baseline; no regression above 2% observed.

Safety and rollout plan: Start as opt-in enterprise feature. Step 1: deploy control-plane component to staging with flag enabled and telemetry ingest in read-only mode. Step 2: enable experimental lanes for 1% traffic on canary cluster for two days; observe metrics; Step 3: gradually expand cohorts and enable replay storage; Step 4: flip default to allow self-serve in Console. Automatic fallback uses a conservative policy (3-sigma p95 latency increase OR 0.5% absolute error-rate jump sustained for 5m). Manual override in Console and CLI remains available.

Migration: Existing rollout manifests are backward compatible. New policy DSL is optional; controllers will fallback to legacy percent-based promotes when no policy provided.

Operational notes: Observability added: exp_lane.* metrics, decision_trace span tags, and a small Console panel under 'Rollouts > Experimental Lanes'. Alerts: exp_lane.fallback.count and exp_lane.replay.failure-rate.

Checklist:
- [x] Controller implementation (policy evaluator + orchestrator)
- [x] Replay writer + S3 archival hooks
- [x] CLI and Console controls for enabling/quarantining lanes
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Benchmarks and perf verification
- [x] Documentation (docs/rollouts/experimental-lanes.md)

Notes: Kept fallback silent by design to avoid user-visible regressions; teams must opt-in to enable replay storage due to storage costs. Related: ENG-2028 (policy DSL), ENG-2101 (telemetry enrichment).
